# Miller Magazine

> > Miller Magazine: Global grain trade, milling technology, and food security intelligence covering wheat markets, agricultural innovation, and industry developments across Black Sea, Turkey, Russia, and international markets.

Miller Magazine provides comprehensive coverage of the global grain and milling industry, featuring market analysis, trade developments, technological innovations, and food security issues. The publication focuses on key producing regions including the Black Sea, Turkey, Russia, China, and Europe, offering insights for millers, traders, and agricultural professionals worldwide.

## Key Topics

- Grain trade and markets
- Food security
- Wheat production and forecasting
- Black Sea grain corridor
- Turkey agriculture and TMO procurement
- Russia grain exports (SovEcon analysis)
- Milling technology and innovation
- Supply chain and logistics
- Agricultural commodity prices
- Regulatory harmonization and EUDR
- Biotechnology in agriculture
- IGC and industry conferences
- FAO food price monitoring
- Geopolitical risks in grain trade
- Women's leadership in milling

- [Acute food insecurity and malnutrition surge for sixth year in a row](https://millermagazine.com/blog/acute-food-insecurity-and-malnutrition-surge-for-sixth-year-in-a-row-6234): Global Report on Food Crises shows sixth consecutive year of rising hunger
- [A new chapter in grain trade: Innovation, unity and resilience for food security](https://millermagazine.com/blog/a-new-chapter-in-grain-trade-innovation-unity-and-resilience-for-food-security-6315): IGC Conference in London on grain trade innovation and food security
- [Agricultural markets 2026: Three consecutive years of weak returns, with reasons for optimism ahead](https://millermagazine.com/blog/agricultural-markets-2026-three-consecutive-years-of-weak-returns-with-reasons-for-optimism-ahead-6557): Peak Trading Research analyzes 2026 agricultural market outlook
- [Küresel gıda fiyatları beş ay sonra yükselişe geçti](https://millermagazine.com/tr/blog/kuresel-gida-fiyatlari-bes-ay-sonra-yukselise-gecti-6670): FAO Food Price Index rises after five months of decline
